This application coming on for orders this day, th e co  following:
 ORDER 01.

This is the third (repeat) application filed by the applicant for grant of regular bail under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 relating to FIR at Crime No.279/2022 registered at P.S- Pithampur, District-Dhar (M.P.) for the offence under sections 363, 366A, 376, 376(2)(n) of IPC and sections 5(L) / 6 of POCSO Act.

The applicant is in custody since 06.02.2023.
02.
As per prosecution story, sister of the Prosecutrix lodged an FIR at P.S. Pithampur by stating that her minor cousin is missing from 26.04.2022.
They tried to search her everywhere but could not find her

During investigation it has been gathered that present applicant on the pretext of marriage abducted the minor prosecutrix, took her with him and kept her for the period of one year Alkesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162287101/
1 and committed repeatedly rape upon her.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the aforementioned offence has been registered against the applicant.
0 3 . Learned counsel for the applicant contended that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this offence.
The applicant is in custody since 06.02.2023.
Prosecutrix has been examined before the trial Court and she was major at the time of incident and went with the applicant.
His earlier two bail applications have been dismissed as withdrawn.
The applicant is a permanent resident of District Dhar.
Final conclusion of trial shall take sufficient long time.

Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions,
as this Court deems fit and proper.
04. Per-contra, learned Government Advocate for respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.
05. Counsel for objector also opposes the prayer and prays for its rejection by submitting that prosecutrix has deposed the present applicant before the trial Court.

06. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case dairy.
07.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties,
nature of allegation as also taking note of the fact that as per the prosecutrix, her date of birth is 21.11.2007.
Prosecutrix herself admits in paragraph no.1 of conviction that she was born in the year 2007, therefore, at the time of incident the Prosecutrix was minor and her consent is immaterial.
Prosecutrix has categorically deposed against the present applicant that this applicant has confined her in a room and committed repeatedly rape upon her.
08. In view of the evidence available on record, this court is not inclined to grant bail to this applicant.
09. Hence, this third bail application filed by applicant under section 439 Cr.P.C. is hereby dismissed.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Divyansh Alkesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162287101/
